title: Name the text to connect to
statement: Ask learners to connect an idea to another text only when the question can name a text they have read; otherwise ask for a prediction framed by the idea.
example: One design judged a question asking for another story with the same idea four units too early, when any story counted.
detail: It is the closing-questions design's rule of thumb for its third question (`grade3-reading/artifacts/feedback-closing-questions-2026-09-24/Closing_Questions_Pattern.txt`). It was written against a closing question asking for another story where someone pretends to be someone they are not: at lesson 1 there is no knowledge web yet, so any story counts, no evidence is required and nothing returns to the text. The other form, a forward prediction framed by the idea, also serves as the next lesson's pre-reading question.

evidence.quote: Rule of thumb: use Form B only when you can name the prior text inside the question. If you cannot name it, use Form A.
At lesson 1 of the year there is no knowledge web yet, so any story counts, no evidence is required, and nothing returns to the text.
